statement: In discrete dynamic programming, backward recursion evaluates value functions $V_t(k)$ backwards in time from terminal condition $V_{T+1}(k) = 0$ to $V_0(k)$ using the Bellman recurrence $V_t(k_t) = \max_{c_t} \left( \ln(c_t) + b V_{t+1}(A k_t^a - c_t) \right)$.

symbols.meaning: Value function representing the optimal value from having capital k at time t
Consumption decision variable at time t
Capital stock state variable at time t
Discount factor for future utility, with 0 < b < 1
Production function exponent parameter, with 0 < a < 1

steps.text: Establish the terminal boundary condition at stage T+1, assuming zero value after the end of the horizon:
Formulate the single-period Bellman equation for each time t in {0, 1, ..., T} by incorporating the capital transition constraint k_{t+1} = A k_t^a - c_t:
Express the backward induction step at period t = T - j using the known value function V_{T-j+1}(k) from the subsequent time step:
Iterate the dynamic programming step backwards from j = 1 (time T) through j = T + 1 to obtain V_0(k), which represents the optimal value of the initial decision problem.

assumptions.assumption: A well-defined terminal state and terminal value function exist (e.g., V_{T+1}(k) = 0).
assumptions.breaks_when: The decision horizon is infinite or terminal boundary conditions are unspecified.

assumptions.assumption: The system state transition rule and stage payoff/cost functions exhibit optimal substructure.
assumptions.breaks_when: Decisions cannot be decomposed into sequential single-period sub-problems.

failure_modes.cause: Attempting backward recursion without specifying a defined final stage T and boundary condition V_{T+1}.
